checksums.name: global_config_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: 16-bit one's complement of the sum of the 6 payload bytes at record offset [2:8]: stored = (0xFFFF - sum(payload)) & 0xFFFF, stored big-endian at record offset [0:2].

checksums.name: global_config_checksum_backup
checksums.formula_detail: Same formula as global_config_checksum, applied to the backup record at offset 0x20.

checksums.name: file_slot_header_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: Self-referential additive 16-bit sum over all 24 bytes of the record with the checksum halfword itself temporarily zeroed, stored big-endian at record offset [14:16].

checksums.name: file_slot_header_checksum_backup
checksums.formula_detail: Same formula as file_slot_header_checksum, applied to the backup record at offset 0xC0.

checksums.name: file_slot_level_data_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: Plain additive 16-bit sum over 0x78 (120) halfwords (240 bytes) of a RAM-staged buffer assembled from the 768-byte EEPROM slot; not a contiguous span of the raw .sav file, so could not be verified against file bytes with the tools available.

io_driver_functions.notes: Generic DMA3 bitstream transfer primitive over the EEPROM serial bus at 0x0D000000; polls a busy bit (& 0x8000) until clear.
EEPROM single-record (8-byte) read: address-select + data-read bit-serial transfer via 0x0813241c, bounds-checks record index against a stored record-count constant.
EEPROM single-record (8-byte) write: wraps the DMA3 write with IRQ-disable/restore (0x08132350/0x081323d8), polls EEPROM write-busy bit at 0x0D000000.
IRQ-disable wrapper used to bracket the EEPROM write's critical section.
Write-verify: reads back the just-written record via 0x0813249c and compares all 4 words; returns non-zero on mismatch.

Write-with-retry: calls 0x0813254c then 0x08132628, retries up to 3 times. No caller found inside the 163 traced functions; reached only via the func_0x08132680(...) pseudo-call syntax from 0x080fb318.
Reads N consecutive 8-byte records, 3 retries per record via func_0x0813249c, aborts via func_0x080fb0d8 on persistent failure.
Writes N consecutive 8-byte records, 3 retries per record via func_0x08132680, aborts via func_0x080fb1a8/func_0x080fb11c on persistent failure.
RAM memset-style clear, used to zero staging buffers before re-read/re-init.
RAM memcpy-style copy, used to stage data between RAM mirror and the record buffer passed to the read/write wrappers.

open_questions: What do the 6 payload bytes of the global config record (offset 0x12-0x17) actually control? Only the checksum mechanics are proven.
What does the constant 0x00004E20 at offset 0x88-0x8B (file-slot header) represent? No derivation relationship found against any other field.
What does the constant 0x00030994 preceding the '0PYA' tag at the start of each file-slot level-data block represent?

What is the exact byte layout of the ~376-byte body of each 768-byte file-slot level-data block (per-level completion flags, item/coin counts, etc.)? All-zero in the only available sample, so no non-zero bytes were available to map.

Is the FUN_080fbc6c (sum of 0x78 halfwords over a staged RAM buffer) checksum verifiable against raw .sav bytes, or does it only ever apply to a RAM-side composite buffer? Needs an emulator RAM trace or paired .ss state, neither of which is present in this workspace's states/ directory.
Does the trailer byte 0x97/0xD7 (observed value 0x03) in the file-slot header actually track the 3-file-slot count, or is that coincidental? No direct writer-to-this-exact-offset was traced.
A second independent .sav sample (ideally with different in-game progress) is needed to separate genuinely constant fields from fields that simply have not changed yet in this single capture.
